graph.name: Planting plans
graph.intro: A long job: first a helper reads the code and splits it into steps, each for a helper, in order. You look over and edit the split before starting; each step merges into the plan's own branch when done, and when all are done you bring the whole into main at once.
graph.goalExample: Such as: add monthly check-in lookups to clock-in, with a page and tests
graph.running: Each step merges into this branch when done; the harvest merges the whole branch into main
graph.splitting: A helper is reading the code and splitting the plan. The split appears here for you to look over before starting.
graph.readingChanges: Looking at what the plan's branch changed…
graph.noSteps: The plan has no steps yet.
graph.acceptanceHint: Acceptance: must fail when written; the last step makes it pass
graph.title: Title
graph.briefHint: Ticket: the goal, where to change, what counts as done
graph.whoHint: Who does it: picked by the rules
graph.checkExample: The check run when done, such as pnpm test (optional)
graph.conflict: Merging into {base} would conflict: {files}. Not bringing it in until the changes on {base} are sorted out.

chat.greeting:
This is the farm chat, where you, the manager and the helpers talk. Tell me a job to do, such as "have the tester run the tests".

Once helpers arrive, write a name like @w1 to call one directly; each job has its ticket thread under it.

phase.off: Type or press the mic to open

chat.label: Farm chat
chat.threadEmpty: Nobody has spoken in this thread yet. Its helper sees what is said here.

chat.newChannelLine: A long-running matter or a project gets a place of its own to talk and send work. Call the manager here and the work is sent here.
chat.name: Channel name
chat.inThread: Say it in the thread; {name} sees it…
chat.toOrchestrator: Tell the manager; @ calls a helper…
chat.toOrchestratorAlone: Just between you and the manager…
chat.stopHint: Stops the manager's round; helpers already sent keep working
